aiExplanation: This function checks whether two **4-character strings** `s1` and `s2` can be equal by comparing their characters at **odd and even positions separately**. It creates four **Sets** to track unique characters: `setOdd1` and `setOdd2` store characters at indices 1 and 3 (odd positions) from each string, while `setEven1` and `setEven2` store characters at indices 0 and 2 (even positions). The loop populates these sets by iterating through indices 0–3, using the bitwise operation `i & 1` to determine if an index is odd or even. Finally, it returns `true` only if both the **odd-position character sets** and **even-position character sets** are identical—meaning they have the same size and contain exactly the same characters—confirming the strings match structurally at their corresponding positions.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function checks if two 4-character strings `s1` and `s2` can be considered **equal under specific swapping rules**. The logic verifies two conditions: for **even positions** (0 and 2), it returns true if either the characters match directly (`s1[0] === s2[0] && s1[2] === s2[2]`) OR they're swapped (`s1[0] === s2[2] && s1[2] === s2[0]`); similarly for **odd positions** (1 and 3), it allows either direct matches or swaps. The function returns `true` only if both conditions are satisfied, meaning the strings are equivalent under these position-swapping rules. Note: there is unreachable dead code after the `return` statement that attempts an alternative approach using Sets to collect characters at odd and even positions, which will never execute.
